bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42510080 (elfutils): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target fuzz-libelf [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42510080
bug_description.normalized:
The staged 608-byte witness is a 64-bit big-endian ELF image whose header makes libelf accept 8 section records at `e_shoff = 0` and later use section 3 as `e_shstrndx`. Because endianness differs from the saved x86_64 build, `file_read_elf()` cannot point directly into the on-file section-header array and instead defers byte-swapping until `elf64_getshdr()` loads the whole table. That deferred conversion turns section 3 into a `SHF_COMPRESSED` `SHT_STRTAB` at file offset `0x200`, leaves section 4 with the out-of-range name offset `0x20202020`, and turns section 5 into a non-`SHF_COMPRESSED` `SHT_SUNW_move` section with `sh_name = 0`, `sh_offset = 0x20`, and `sh_size = 0x1c`.

On the saved crashing pass (`LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput:82` in both saved traces), libelf first mishandles section 3 in `elf_compress()`: `compressed = (sh_flags & SHF_COMPRESSED)` evaluates to `0x800`, so the buggy test `compressed == 1` does not reject an already-compressed section. `elf_getdata()` classifies section 3 as `ELF_T_CHDR`; the special `Elf64_cvt_chdr()` helper copies all 96 bytes, letting libelf recompress the whole shstrtab into a self-consistent in-memory compressed section. A later `elf_strptr(elf, 3, 0)` therefore yields a non-NULL `.z...` name for section 5, and the harness branch in `fuzz_logic_one()` consumes that value to call `elf_compress_gnu(scn, 0, 0)` on section 5.

For section 5, `__libelf_set_rawdata_wrlock()` admits `sh_size = 28` as exactly one external `Elf64_Ext_Move`, `convert_data()` allocates a 28-byte heap buffer, and `__elf_xfctstom[ELFCLASS64 - 1][ELF_T_MOVE]` resolves to `Elf64_cvt_Move`. The vulnerable `START / END` macro in `libelf/gelf_xlate.c` counts native `Elf64_Move` records, so on the saved x86_64 build `sizeof (Elf64_Move) = 32` and `len = 28` gives zero loop iterations with no fallback copy. `convert_data()` then publishes the untouched allocation as `data->d_buf`, and `elf_compress_gnu()` executes `memcmp(data->d_buf, "ZLIB", 4)` because `data->d_size` is 28, producing the saved MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value report. The patch adds `size_t sz` plus `if (len % sz > 0) memmove (dest, src, len % sz);`, which copies the 28-byte remainder for this exact dispatch and removes the undefined read.

source.description: Source. libelf first materializes the attacker-controlled section-count and section-table offset fields from the big-endian ELF header into host-endian local state.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` begins with a 64-bit big-endian ELF header (`EI_CLASS = ELFCLASS64`, `EI_DATA = ELFDATA2MSB`). At this statement the header bytes decode to `e_shnum = 8` and `e_shoff = 0`; later `file_read_elf()` copies `e_shstrndx = 3` from the same header. Those exact values are what make libelf treat the first 512 bytes of the file as eight section headers and later resolve section names through section 3.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: MSAN sink. This GNU-header check reaches `memcmp(data->d_buf, "ZLIB", 4)`, which reads the first four bytes of the translated section-5 buffer after `convert_data()` published a 28-byte heap allocation that `Elf64_cvt_Move` left untouched.
sink.note: Both `default_crash_trace.txt` and `sanitizer_trace.txt` place the top project frame at `libelf/elf_compress_gnu.c:155` in `elf_compress_gnu()` with a `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` summary in `memcmp`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The shared xlate macro iterates in units of the native `Elf64_Move` size, but this witness was admitted as a single 28-byte external `Elf64_Ext_Move` record. For the exact `Elf64_cvt_Move` dispatch reached here, `len` is 28 and `sizeof (Elf64_Move)` is 32 on the saved x86_64 build, so the loop count is zero and the vulnerable converter returns without writing any bytes to the freshly allocated destination buffer.
root_cause.note: The selected dispatch arm is exact: `__elf_xfctstom[ELFCLASS64 - 1][ELF_T_MOVE] = Elf64_cvt_Move`. `patch.diff` adds `size_t sz` and `if (len % sz > 0) memmove (dest, src, len % sz);` after this loop; for this witness `len % sz` is 28, so the patched converter copies the whole buffer even though `n` is 0.

fine_trace.note: Source. The big-endian 64-bit ELF header is first materialized into host-endian libelf state here. For the staged witness this yields `e_shnum = 8` and `e_shoff = 0`, the two header fields that drive how many section records exist and where libelf later reads them from.

libelf adopts `result = 8` as the section count. Because `e_shnum` is nonzero, it does not take the extended-count fallback through section 0; later code will treat the file as having exactly eight section slots.

fine_trace.code: elf->state.elf64.ehdr = memcpy (&elf->state.elf64.ehdr_mem, e_ident, sizeof (Elf64_Ehdr)); ... CONVERT (elf->state.elf64.ehdr_mem.e_shoff); ... CONVERT (elf->state.elf64.ehdr_mem.e_shstrndx);
fine_trace.note: file_read_elf preserves the same witness header in `elf->state.elf64.ehdr`, adding `e_shstrndx = 3` to the already-converted `e_shoff = 0`. Those stored header fields later guide both the shstrtab lookup and every deferred section-header load.

Because the file byte order does not match the host, `file_read_elf()` cannot install direct `Elf64_Shdr *` pointers yet. Instead it creates eight section shells indexed `0..7`; later `elf64_getshdr()` resolves those indexes into converted section headers.

fine_trace.note: The first later `elf64_getshdr()` call loads and byte-swaps all 8 section headers from file offset `e_shoff = 0` into host-endian `Elf64_Shdr` records, then installs them into the section slots. This is where libelf makes the later-relevant header values explicit: section 3 becomes `SHT_STRTAB`, `sh_offset = 0x200`, `sh_size = 0x60`, `sh_flags` including `SHF_COMPRESSED`; section 4 keeps `sh_name = 0x20202020`; section 5 becomes `sh_name = 0`, `SHT_SUNW_move`, `sh_offset = 0x20`, `sh_size = 0x1c`, and no `SHF_COMPRESSED`.
libelf reads the stored ELF header field `e_shstrndx` and returns `3`, fixing section 3 as the string-table section for later `elf_strptr()` name lookups.

fine_trace.note: When `elf_getdata()` is pulled on section 3, libelf materializes the converted shstrtab header fields `offset = 0x200`, `size = 0x60`, `type = SHT_STRTAB`, `align = 0x2000000000000000`, and `flags` with `SHF_COMPRESSED` from section slot 3.

Because section 3 still carries `SHF_COMPRESSED`, libelf reclassifies its bytes as `ELF_T_CHDR` rather than plain string-table bytes. That exact type choice selects the special `Elf64_cvt_chdr()` helper for the later `elf_getdata()` conversion.

fine_trace.code: if (dest != src) memmove (dest, src, len); if (len >= sizeof (Elf64_Chdr)) Elf64_cvt_Chdr (dest, src, sizeof (Elf64_Chdr), encode);
fine_trace.note: The `ELF_T_CHDR` converter copies all `len` bytes and only byte-swaps the first 24-byte header. For section 3, that means `elf_getdata()` hands `elf_compress()` the entire 96-byte byte image, preserving the leading `.z` bytes and the trailing NUL terminator instead of dropping the payload after the header.

fine_trace.note: For section 3, `compressed = (sh_flags & SHF_COMPRESSED)` becomes `0x800`, so the buggy test `compressed == 1` is false and the already-compressed shstrtab is recompressed instead of being rejected. libelf compresses the full 96-byte image from step 9, prepends a valid `Elf64_Chdr`, and replaces section 3's rawdata with that self-consistent compressed buffer.

When section names are later resolved through string-table index 3, section 3 is now a valid compressed section. `get_zdata()` therefore inflates the step-10 buffer back into a 96-byte `zdata_base` that matches the original shstrtab bytes from file offset `0x200`.

When later code resolves section 5's name, `elf_strptr(elf, 3, 0)` uses the shstrtab index from step 5 and the section-5 name offset from step 4. The inflated table from step 11 makes `result = &strscn->zdata_base[0]`, whose first bytes are `.z`; section 4's converted `sh_name = 0x20202020` still stays out of range, so section 5 is the first later section whose name lookup yields a non-NULL `.z...` pointer.

fine_trace.note: On section 5, the harness sees `(shdr->sh_flags & SHF_COMPRESSED) == 0` from step 4, `name != NULL` from step 12, and the leading bytes `'.'` and `'z'`, so this branch calls `elf_compress_gnu(scn, 0, 0)` on that same section.

fine_trace.note: Inside the step-13 `elf_compress_gnu()` call, libelf materializes the converted section-5 header values `offset = 32`, `size = 28`, `type = 0x6ffffffa (SHT_SUNW_move)`, `align = 0xffffffff20202020`, and `flags = 0x2020202020202020` from section slot 5.

fine_trace.code: Elf_Type t = shtype_map[TYPEIDX (type)]; ... entsize = __libelf_type_sizes[elf->class - 1][t]; ... if (unlikely (size % entsize != 0))
fine_trace.note: The section-5 admission logic maps `type = SHT_SUNW_move` to `t = ELF_T_MOVE` and computes the external record size from `exttypes.h`. For ELFCLASS64, `Elf64_Ext_Move` is 28 bytes, so `size = 28` is accepted as exactly one external MOVE record instead of being rejected as malformed.

fine_trace.code: ssize_t n = pread_retry (elf->fildes, scn->rawdata.d.d_buf, size, elf->start_offset + offset);
fine_trace.note: Using `offset = 32` and `size = 28`, libelf reads the exact 28-byte section-5 body from file bytes `[0x20, 0x3c)` into `scn->rawdata.d.d_buf`.

Because section 5 does not carry `SHF_COMPRESSED`, libelf classifies it through `__libelf_data_type(ehdr, type, align)` instead of forcing `ELF_T_CHDR`. With `type = SHT_SUNW_move`, this stores `scn->rawdata.d.d_type = ELF_T_MOVE`.

This fast-path predicate is false on the witness. The file is big-endian (`EI_DATA = ELFDATA2MSB` from step 2), the saved x86_64 build uses `MY_ELFDATA = ELFDATA2LSB`, and step 17 stored `type = ELF_T_MOVE`, so `convert_data()` must take the structured xlate branch instead of the raw-byte copy or alias path.

MSAN allocation origin. `convert_data()` allocates a fresh 28-byte destination buffer for the translated section-5 data, and `malloc` leaves all 28 bytes uninitialized until a later write defines them.

fine_trace.var: fp, eclass, type, scn->data_base, rawdata_source, size
fine_trace.note: With `eclass = ELFCLASS64` and `type = ELF_T_MOVE`, `fp` resolves exactly to `Elf64_cvt_Move`, and `convert_data()` calls that converter with `len = 28` on the fresh heap buffer from step 19.

Root cause. `Elf64_cvt_Move` counts in units of the native `Elf64_Move` type, not the 28-byte external `Elf64_Ext_Move` that step 15 used for admission. On the saved x86_64 build `sizeof (Elf64_Move)` is 32, so with `len = 28` the loop computes `n = 0`, executes zero iterations, and this vulnerable revision has no fallback `memmove`; none of `dest[0..27]` are written.

fine_trace.code: scn->data_list.data.d.d_buf = scn->data_base; scn->data_list.data.d.d_size = size; scn->data_list.data.d.d_type = type;
fine_trace.note: After `Elf64_cvt_Move` returns, `convert_data()` publishes the same untouched 28-byte heap allocation as the first `Elf_Data` record returned by `elf_getdata()`.

Sink. On this witness `data->d_size` is 28, so `data->d_size < 12` is false and `memcmp(data->d_buf, "ZLIB", 4)` executes. That read consumes `data->d_buf[0..3]` from the untouched heap buffer published at step 22, matching the saved MSAN report of uninitialized bytes at offset 0 inside the 4-byte `memcmp` region.

allocation_context.note: MSAN says the uninitialized bytes were created by heap allocation at this line; fine-trace step 20 is the exact `Elf64_cvt_Move` dispatch and step 21 is the zero-iteration case that leaves that 28-byte allocation untouched before `memcmp` consumes it at step 23.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch changes the shared xlate macro in `libelf/gelf_xlate.c` to compute `sz` and copy any `len % sz` remainder with `memmove`. For the exact `Elf64_cvt_Move` dispatch on this witness, `len` is 28 and `sz = sizeof (Elf64_Move)` is 32, so the patched fallback copies all 28 bytes and prevents the later `memcmp` at fine-trace step 23 from reading poison.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. Fine-trace step 23 is the exact `elf_compress_gnu.c:155` call site named by both saved crash traces.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. MSAN attributes the poison to the heap allocation at `convert_data:168` (fine-trace step 19), and fine-trace steps 20 through 22 show the exact `Elf64_cvt_Move` path where `len = 28` yields zero loop iterations and leaves that allocation wholly uninitialized before step 23 consumes it.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved crash stack `memcmp -> elf_compress_gnu -> fuzz_logic_one -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` matches the reachability chain through the explicit harness gate in steps 12 and 13 and the sink in step 23, while the allocation stack `convert_data -> __libelf_set_data_list_rdlock -> __elf_getdata_rdlock -> elf_getdata -> elf_compress_gnu` is reflected by steps 18 through 23.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. Steps 0 through 5 consume the ELF header, admit eight section records, convert the section table, and fix `e_shstrndx = 3`. Steps 6 through 12 use the converted section-3 and section-5 headers to turn section 3 into a valid in-memory compressed shstrtab and then recover the non-NULL `.z...` name for section 5. Step 13 is the harness predicate and call that consumes that name to invoke `elf_compress_gnu()` on section 5. Steps 14 through 17 import section 5's header/body and classify it as `ELF_T_MOVE`; steps 18 through 22 allocate a destination buffer, dispatch `Elf64_cvt_Move`, leave all 28 bytes undefined, and publish that buffer as `data->d_buf`; step 23 reads bytes `0..3` in `memcmp`.

format.name: Exact staged 608-byte ELF witness
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged 608-byte file at `gt_results/arvo_42510080/poc`; no broader input class is claimed. The witness must remain a 64-bit big-endian ELF file whose header decodes to `e_shoff = 0`, `e_shnum = 8`, and `e_shstrndx = 3`, so libelf treats the first 512 bytes as eight section headers and later resolves names through section 3. Within that exact layout, section 3 must stay a `SHF_COMPRESSED` `SHT_STRTAB` with `sh_offset = 0x200` and `sh_size = 0x60`, section 4 must keep the out-of-range name offset `0x20202020`, and section 5 must stay a non-`SHF_COMPRESSED` `SHT_SUNW_move` section with `sh_name = 0`, `sh_offset = 0x20`, and `sh_size = 0x1c`. That exact combination makes section 3 become a valid in-memory compressed shstrtab before section 5 is named, then drives section 5 into the `Elf64_cvt_Move` zero-iteration case before `memcmp(data->d_buf, "ZLIB", 4)`.
